terms.title: Being
terms.definition: That in terms of which entities are intelligible as beings; not itself another entity.
terms.nuance: The initial question of Being must not be confused with the existence of a supreme object.

terms.title: entity / being
terms.definition: Whatever is, considered as an entity; distinct in Heidegger’s analysis from Being.
terms.nuance: “Beings” and “entities” are translation strategies; each has virtues and costs.

terms.title: Dasein
terms.definition: The entity each of us is, for whom its Being is an issue.
terms.nuance: Literally there-being; not simply a Cartesian ego or biological human organism.

terms.title: ontic
terms.definition: Concerning factual entities and their determinate characteristics.
terms.nuance: The ontic/ontological contrast is methodological, not a ranking of dignity.

terms.title: ontological
terms.definition: Concerning Being, modes of Being and their structures.
terms.nuance: Ontological analysis should not be confused with cataloguing properties.

terms.title: ontological difference
terms.definition: The distinction between Being and beings/entities.
terms.nuance: A central Heideggerian distinction, increasingly explicit in works beyond the introduction to Being and Time.

terms.title: ontology
terms.definition: Inquiry into Being and the structures by which entities are intelligible.
terms.nuance: Fundamental ontology aims to clarify the horizon of the meaning of Being.

terms.title: existence
terms.definition: For Heidegger, the mode of Being in which Dasein lives its possibilities.
terms.nuance: Distinct from a bare fact that a thing occurs or is present.

terms.title: everydayness
terms.definition: The ordinary, average ways Dasein is engaged in its world.
terms.nuance: A methodological starting point, not merely an ethical criticism of daily routine.

terms.title: worldhood
terms.definition: The existential structure of a meaningful world of references and involvement.
terms.nuance: Not simply the sum of all things in physical space.

terms.title: understanding
terms.definition: Dasein’s projection of possibilities; an existential way of being able to be.
terms.nuance: More primary than a purely theoretical comprehension of propositions.

terms.title: temporality
terms.definition: The ecstatic structure of Dasein’s Being developed as its ontological meaning.
terms.nuance: Not reducible to succession of now-points or clock time.

terms.title: Zeitlichkeit
terms.definition: Temporality: the temporal structure of Dasein’s Being.
terms.nuance: Sometimes distinguished in translation from Temporalität, concerning Being as such.

terms.title: Temporalität
terms.definition: The more general temporal horizon projected for interpreting the meaning of Being.
terms.nuance: Distinguish from Zeitlichkeit; the project is unfinished in the published Being and Time.

terms.title: Destruktion
terms.definition: Critical dismantling and retrieval of inherited ontological concepts.
terms.nuance: A constructive historical inquiry, not indiscriminate demolition.

terms.title: phenomenon
terms.definition: That which shows itself from itself; methodological focus of phenomenology.
terms.nuance: Heidegger distinguishes self-showing from merely seeming and from appearance as indication.

terms.title: logos
terms.definition: Discourse or articulation; in Heidegger’s methodological account, letting something be seen.
terms.nuance: Its semantic range in Greek is considerably wider than any single English equivalent.

terms.title: hermeneutics
terms.definition: Interpretation as the method through which structures of meaning are articulated.
terms.nuance: Foregrounding interpretation does not license unfalsifiable speculation.

terms.title: intentionality
terms.definition: The directedness of consciousness toward something as intended.
terms.nuance: Directedness is not necessarily a causal relation between two independent objects.

terms.title: natural attitude
terms.definition: The everyday stance in which a surrounding world is tacitly taken to exist.
terms.nuance: Phenomenology describes rather than simply condemns this attitude.

terms.title: epoché
terms.definition: Methodological suspension of the natural attitude’s existential positing.
terms.nuance: Bracketing is not a proof that the world fails to exist.

terms.title: phenomenological reduction
terms.definition: The methodological reorientation toward appearing and its intentional conditions.
terms.nuance: Multiple senses and stages occur throughout Husserl’s work.

terms.title: transcendental
terms.definition: Concerning conditions of the possibility and intelligibility of experience and objectivity.
terms.nuance: Not synonymous with mystical or supernatural.

terms.title: constitution
terms.definition: Articulation of the structures through which object-sense and validity arise in intentional life.
terms.nuance: Does not straightforwardly mean physically creating objects.

terms.title: noesis
terms.definition: Intentional lived act considered in its act-character.
terms.nuance: Distinguish from noema, the correlate as intended.

terms.title: noema
terms.definition: Object as intended in its sense and manner of givenness.
terms.nuance: Whether noema is content, object-as-intended or a special correlate is debated.

terms.title: horizon
terms.definition: The background of implicit co-intentions and possibilities accompanying what appears.
terms.nuance: Only one side of a material thing may be perceived while more is intended.

terms.title: lifeworld
terms.definition: World of everyday lived meaning prior to specialized theoretical abstractions.
terms.nuance: Especially prominent in Husserl’s later writings and related post-Husserlian thought.

terms.title: lived body
terms.definition: The body as the situated subject of perception and action, not merely a physical object.
terms.nuance: Merleau-Ponty distinguishes lived corporeality from treating the body as inert thing.

terms.title: perception
terms.definition: Bodily openness to a meaningful field in Merleau-Ponty’s phenomenology.
terms.nuance: Not equivalent to passive reception of sensory data.

terms.title: pre-reflective experience
terms.definition: Lived experience as operative before explicit reflective judgment.
terms.nuance: Prior does not have to mean temporally earlier.

terms.title: sensation
terms.definition: An allegedly elementary sensory unit criticized as the starting point of perception.
terms.nuance: Physiological input and phenomenal organization answer distinct questions.

terms.title: Gestalt
terms.definition: Organized form or figure-ground structure irreducible to an inventory of atoms.
terms.nuance: A major influence from Gestalt psychology, transformed phenomenologically.

terms.title: attention
terms.definition: A transformation or reorganization of the perceptual field.
terms.nuance: Not merely a beam of awareness directed at fixed data.
